_comment: Proposed fixes for Miami: shown as the infographic timeline on miami/index.html.
Hand-curated. Review about once a quarter: update status, cost, and outcome, add new projects.
date      YYYY-MM-DD (or YYYY-MM-01 / YYYY-01-01 when only month or year is known)
summary   one or two plain sentences: what it is
status    Planned | In design | In progress | Completed | Revised | On hold
cost      { usd: number, label: text shown on the page }
outcome   what it does or has done, in plain words
sources   at least one { name, url }. Entries without a source are skipped.

items.title: Shorecrest South flood improvements
items.summary: New and larger storm drains, injection wells, and a stormwater pump station that empties into the Little River Canal, plus rebuilt roads.
items.outcome: Built to relieve street flooding for 327 properties worth about $264M. Phase I construction July 2026 to March 2027; Phase II through May 2029.

items.title: Brickell Bay Drive seawall and road
items.summary: New seawall, bay walk, rebuilt road, and drainage along Brickell Bay Drive from SE 14th Street to SE 15th Road.
items.outcome: Protects about 787 homes and $316M in property value from storm surge and rising seas. Construction expected February 2027 to January 2029.

items.title: Back Bay storm surge plan, revised
items.summary: The Army Corps of Engineers' redrawn plan drops the floodwall. It elevates about 2,100 homes, floodproofs about 400 critical buildings like fire stations and shelters, and studies reefs and mangroves.
items.outcome: Sent to Congress for authorization in 2024. Federally funded if approved; not yet built.

items.title: Miami Stormwater Master Plan
items.summary: A 40-year plan for giant pumps, miles of 6-foot seawalls, thousands of injection wells, and 8-foot underground pipes.
items.outcome: Aims to keep Miami livable largely as it is through 2060. The city says it will not keep every neighborhood dry.

items.title: Back Bay floodwall plan
items.summary: The Army Corps' first plan: a mile-long floodwall along Biscayne Bay and flood gates across the Miami River, Little River, and Biscayne Canal.
items.outcome: Rejected by residents and the county. In 2022 the Corps agreed to redo it with more natural protection.

items.title: Miami Forever Bond
items.summary: Voters approved a $400M bond. The biggest share, $192M, is set aside for sea level rise and flood prevention.
items.outcome: By late 2025 only about $30M (16%) of the flood money had been spent. Officials cite delays, lost grants, and changing plans.
